_comment: Every way a menu can end up a given size, written as one file: nothing outside refers to these entries or the menus behind them, so each is inline rather than a pair of files to cross-reference. Inline menus are validated at load just like named ones, which is why the oversized case still warns. Open the main menu under a theme with /game menu open testmod:main <theme> and walk in. The theme is inherited, so every case is drawn in the style you started with.
title: Sizing cases

menu._comment: No size given and only two entries, so it asks for a single row and the container comes out as short as the theme allows: 2 rows under the default, 3 under testmod:debug, 1 under testmod:plain.
menu.title: Tiny

menu._comment: The same two entries as Tiny, but asking for a 9:4 region outright. It keeps that shape however few entries it holds, and the theme's chrome is added around it.
menu.title: Sized 9:4

menu._comment: The game decides what shares a line, the theme spaces and centres them. Three declared rows means a 3-row region.
menu.title: Rows

menu._comment: Asks for a single row it cannot possibly hold, so the page controls appear and the container still comes out as short as the region plus the theme's chrome. Overflow a layout can page is not an error and is not logged.
menu.title: Paged

menu._comment: Asks for the whole of the tallest vanilla container, leaving no room for chrome. Only testmod:plain can honour it; every other theme cuts it down and says so in the log at datapack load. That warning is the point of this entry. Written as an object rather than "9:6" to show the long form of a size.
menu.title: Oversized 9:6
